question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient allowlist for Slack message sends now, and should that policy be Slack-specific channel config or part of a shared human-chat outbound target policy?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but adding `allowTo` changes public config and outbound authorization semantics under a documented trusted-operator model, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary by itself.

options.title: Add Shared Outbound Target Policy
options.body: Add a documented allowTo-style outbound recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and shared enforcement before durable/gateway sends while keeping `allowFrom` inbound-only.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Guardrails
options.body: Track Slack recipient allowlisting as an acceptance case under #87870 so sanitizer, verified delivery, and target authorization are designed together.

options.title: Decline Core AllowTo For Now
options.body: Keep the current trusted-operator model and rely on agent/tool/process policy, documenting that `dmPolicy` and `allowFrom` do not constrain explicit operator sends.

recommendation.title: Add Shared Outbound Target Policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented allowTo-style outbound recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and shared enforcement before durable/gateway sends while keeping `allowFrom` inbound-only.

likelyOwner.reason: The Slack allowlist/security history and related product/security triage make this the best available owner for the config boundary decision.
